business_quality_reasoning: BPM Electrical has traded since 2015 with full accounts filed — an established, stable electrician rather than a startup. Only 8 Google reviews though, and the emergency call-out positioning suggests job-value rather than contract-scale revenue.
price_point_reasoning: Emergency call-outs plus domestic work (rewires, consumer units, lighting) suggest a typical job value around £150-£300.
modernity_gap: The underlying site is genuinely modern — dark theme, clear typography, structured service sections — but an aggressive emergency-callout interstitial blocks and re-appears over the content, wrecking the experience.
site_weaknesses: A 'Need an emergency electrician?' modal gates the whole page and appears repeatedly as you scroll — visitors cannot browse without dismissing it
The interstitial dominates the mobile view too, covering the hero entirely
Only 8 Google reviews are earned but none are displayed on the site
NICEIC accreditation is mentioned in small text but not presented as a proper credibility block with logos or certificate detail
No pricing guidance, response-time promise detail or named engineer — the page sells urgency but not trust
site_analysis: This is the rare prospect with a modern site: dark, sharp design with well-organised sections covering emergency work, rewiring, lighting, consumer units and commercial. The big flaw is a full-screen emergency interstitial that blocks the content and repeats down the page — the site's own best material is hidden behind a popup. Fixing the gate and adding real reviews would lift conversion without a rebuild.
review_summary: Your site actually looks sharp, but a 'Need an emergency electrician?' popup covers the whole page and keeps coming back as visitors scroll — people have to fight it just to see what you offer. Your NICEIC accreditation and reviews barely get a look in. Letting the content breathe would do more for you than the popup does.
outreach_angle: Your site hides a genuinely good design behind an emergency-callout popup that reappears down the whole page — visitors never see your best content.
